issues.description: The UML in the problem statement indicates the Lecture attributes are private ( '-' ), and the solution defines these fields as private, but the template declares at least two fields as public (lectureName and numberOfInscribedStudents). This visibility mismatch can confuse students about the intended encapsulation (whether to make fields private and use getters/setters) and may lead them to skip implementing the required getters/setters or implement them inconsistently.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the attribute declarations in the template Lecture.java to be private (matching the UML and the solution) and rely on the getters/setters for access. For example, declare private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; and add the remaining private fields. This preserves encapsulation and aligns the template with the specification and solution.
